2. Petitioner instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 72 of 2013 for realization of Tk. 1,33,57.49,459.00 (One hundred thirty three crore fifty seven lacy forty nine thousand four Hundred and fifty nine). The Artha Rin Adalat by its judgment and order dated 17.09.2013 decreed the suit in preliminary form. 

 3. The judgment debtor did not file any appeal or application for setting aside is ex-party decree by depositing the statutory deposit. She filed the above writ petition and the High Court Division by impugned judgment set-aside the ex-parte decree. It has held that there was no proper service of the summons upon the writ petitioner and that the ex-parte decree was passed without following the procedures of the service of summons. 

 4. Whether or not the summons were duly served upon the writ petitioner is a disputed fact which cannot be looked in by the High Court Division in a summary filed under Article 102(2) of the Constitution. Moreso this Division has already held that no writ petition is maintainable challenging the decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, in as much as, the remedy against the ex-parte decree is provided in Ain itself. The High Court Division has overlooked the law settled by this Division. The judgment of the High Court Division is set-aside.
